article.headline: Wednesday National Lottery Jackpot Hits 2.8 Million Pounds for Lucky Ticket Holders
article.summary: The National Lottery held its Lotto and Thunderball draws on Wednesday, October 28, offering players a top prize of 2.8 million pounds.
article.body:
A life-changing 2.8 million pounds was the headline jackpot available for players participating in this Wednesday's National Lottery draw. This significant prize pool offered participants the potential to clear debts, fund travel, or contribute to charitable causes.

For those who play, the stakes reach beyond personal gain as the National Lottery generates approximately 30 million pounds every week for good causes across the United Kingdom. With a cost of 2 pounds per play, the system provides two distinct opportunities to win per entry following recent updates to the game structure.

According to Chronicle Live, the schedule for the evening featured the primary Lotto draw at 8pm, followed immediately by the Thunderball draw at 8.15pm. These drawings represent one of the recurring weekly opportunities for individuals to participate in the nationwide event.

Players checking their tickets for Wednesday, October 28, are encouraged by The Independent to refresh their digital platforms or official sources to verify the specific winning number combinations for both the Lotto and Thunderball games. No further announcements regarding future jackpot adjustments were provided at this time.

article.headline: Riquelme Fillipi snatches 90th-minute equalizer to rescue Inter Miami against Cincinnati
article.summary: Inter Miami and FC Cincinnati fought to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday as Riquelme Fillipi scored in the final minute to share the points.
article.body: Riquelme Fillipi emerged from the bench in the 83rd minute to salvage a point for Inter Miami, firing home a crucial equalizer in the 90th minute. The dramatic finish followed a frantic second-half turnaround that saw all four goals scored in the final 30 minutes of play at Nu Stadium. Following a scoreless first half that saw Lionel Messi receive a yellow card in the 44th minute, Luis Suarez broke the deadlock in the 61st minute off an assist from Casemiro. The opening goal electrified the home crowd, but Miami’s lead proved short-lived as Cincinnati shifted the momentum late in the match. The visitors capitalized on a tiring defense, with Kenji Mboma Dem leveling the score in the 80th minute. Just six minutes later, Samuel Gidi connected on a Tyler Barlow assist to put Cincinnati ahead 2-1, silencing the Florida supporters. Facing a potential defeat, Inter Miami maintained pressure until Fillipi converted a delivery from Rodrigo De Paul in the dying moments of regulation. The draw highlights a test for Miami as they continue their Eastern Conference campaign, while Cincinnati’s late surge underscores their desperate pursuit of a playoff position. Goal.com reports that despite the offensive flurry, disciplinary issues plagued Miami, resulting in three separate yellow cards during the match. With the result finalized at 2-2, both teams leave the pitch having traded leads in a match defined by second-half chaos. While Suarez and Fillipi proved decisive for the hosts, the team now looks to regain defensive stability following a difficult night where they conceded two goals in quick succession.
